sections.title: Concept of One Word Substitution (Level 2)
sections.content: In Level 2, the words are slightly less common and their meanings often need to be understood through their roots or suffixes. Step 1: Identify the main idea of the phrase. Step 2: Look at the suffix or root of the word (such as cracy, archy, ary, etc.). Step 3: Compare the meanings of the options. Step 4: Choose the word that gives the most precise meaning as the correct one word substitution.

sections.title: Types of Government (Cracy / Archy)
sections.content: Step 1: Identify what type of government or rule is being described. Step 2: Check whether the word ends with 'cracy' or 'archy', which indicate a system of rule. Step 3: Understand the type of government from the root word. Step 4: Select the correct word. Examples: Oligarchy = rule by a few people, Theocracy = rule by religious leaders, Anarchy = absence of government, Gerontocracy = rule by elderly people.

sections.title: Places and Collections
sections.content: Step 1: Check whether the phrase refers to a place or a collection. Step 2: Identify the object or creature involved. Step 3: Recognize the word that represents the related place. Step 4: Understand the difference between similar-looking words. Examples: Aviary = a place for birds, Apiary = a place for bees, Arsenal = a store of weapons, Granary = a storehouse for grain, Sanatorium = a place for the treatment of sick people.

sections.title: Human Habits and Nature
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the person's behavior or nature. Step 2: Understand the meaning through the root word. Step 3: Pay attention to differences between similar words. Step 4: Choose the word that best matches the behavior. Examples: Egoist = a person who prioritizes self-interest, Egotist = a person who talks excessively about himself, Misanthrope = a person who hates or dislikes humankind.

sections.title: Religious and Social Terms
sections.content: Step 1: Identify whether the word relates to religion or social belief. Step 2: Recognize the root word. Step 3: Compare the meanings. Step 4: Choose the correct word. Examples: Polygamy = the practice of having more than one spouse, Atheist = a person who does not believe in God, Blasphemy = speaking disrespectfully about God or religion.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Confusing words with similar spellings. 2. Ignoring suffixes like cracy, archy, and ary. 3. Choosing answers without understanding the root meaning.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 2, suffixes and root meanings are very important. 'Cracy/Archy' indicate systems of government, 'ary' often indicates a place or collection, and many words relate to human nature or religious beliefs.

tricks.title: Archy = Rule Trick
tricks.explanation: 'Archy' also refers to rule or control.
tricks.example: Oligarchy = rule by a few people.

tricks.title: Ary = Place Trick
tricks.explanation: 'Ary' often represents a place or collection.

tricks.title: Bee vs Bird Memory
tricks.explanation: Apiary is for bees and Aviary is for birds.

tricks.title: Self Words Difference
tricks.explanation: Egoist prioritizes self-interest, while Egotist talks excessively about himself.

tricks.title: Human Hate Trick
tricks.explanation: Misanthrope is a person who hates or dislikes humans.
tricks.example: A person who dislikes people → Misanthrope.

tricks.title: Religion Belief Trick
tricks.explanation: Atheist is someone who does not believe in God.
tricks.example: Someone who does not believe in God → Atheist.

tricks.title: Multiple Marriage Trick
tricks.explanation: Polygamy means having more than one spouse.
tricks.example: One person having multiple spouses → Polygamy.
